html:
Leo III was Byzantine emperor from 717 to 741 and the founder of the Isaurian dynasty. Born in Germanikeia in northern Syria around 685, he rose as a soldier under Justinian II and later commanded the Anatolic theme.

He seized the throne in March 717, ending the Twenty Years' Anarchy. Months later a huge Umayyad army and fleet arrived at the walls. His defence in the second Arab siege, helped by Greek fire, a hard winter and Bulgar allies, saved Constantinople. In 740 he beat the Arabs at Akroinon in Anatolia.

At home he issued the Ecloga, a short law book in Greek. He is also linked with the start of iconoclasm, the ban on holy images, though how far he went is debated, since most accounts were written by his enemies. His son Constantine V pushed the policy much harder.
sum: Leo III was Byzantine emperor from 717 to 741 and the founder of the Isaurian dynasty. Born in Germanikeia in northern Syria around 685, he rose as a soldier under Justinian II and later commanded the Anatolic theme.
